Topic: UK small business AI use has more than doubled this year, to 47%
Caption Notes: Nearly half of UK small business owners are now using AI — up from just 22% a year ago, according to a new Simply Business survey. Most are using it to write content, solve problems and cut down on admin. But only one in five feel truly confident with it, and security worries are still holding a lot of people back. Topic: California just passed the toughest AI chatbot law yet, to protect kids
Caption Notes: California has signed the strictest child-safety law yet for AI chatbots, named after a teenager who died after months of conversations with ChatGPT. From 2027, chatbot makers there must verify users' ages, spot signs of self-harm in under-18s, alert parents and pass independent safety audits. It's a US law, but the same chatbots are used by teenagers here too. If your child chats with AI, it's worth checking what safety settings the apps they use already offer. Topic: Northern Ireland man loses £250,000 to an AI deepfake investment scam
Caption Notes: A man in Northern Ireland has lost £250,000 after scammers used an AI-generated video of a well-known financial personality to promote a fake investment. He was then messaged on WhatsApp, talked into paying more, and even gave the scammers remote access to his computer. Police say this kind of fraud is getting harder to spot because the fake videos look so real. If a video seems to show someone recommending an investment, check directly with that person or company before sending any money. Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI safety updates.
